summary: LSU beat Louisiana Tech 45-14 despite four first-half turnovers. The trip to Ole Miss makes ball security the priority. Watch Leavitt’s decisions near the goal line and whether the defensive pressure travels to Oxford.

items.headline: Leavitt threw three interceptions, two in the red zone
items.tldr: Watch the decision when the first scoring option is covered. Keeping a possession alive matters more than forcing a touchdown throw.

items.headline: Umanmielen recorded three sacks against Louisiana Tech
items.tldr: Watch whether the defensive front can disrupt the pocket while keeping its lanes. A free scramble can undo otherwise effective pressure.

items.headline: Chambliss completed 23 of 26 passes against Charlotte
items.tldr: Watch the underneath coverage as closely as the pass rush. Making the quarterback hold the ball would give pressure time to arrive.

items.headline: Construction changes the route around The Grove
items.tldr: Check the revised pickup and dropoff directions before driving into Oxford. Plan the approach to campus as well as the parking spot.

items.headline: SEC said discussions would continue after Thursday’s meeting
items.tldr: The statement did not announce a resolution. Keep the dated conference update separate from assumptions about this week’s roster or game.

lead.headline: Keep the ball in Oxford.
lead.body: Watch Leavitt’s decisions when space gets tight. A throw away can preserve a scoring chance; a forced pass can give the opponent the next possession.

matchup.question: What matters most at Ole Miss?
matchup.answer: Protect the ball near the goal line, make the opposing quarterback work past his first read, and keep defensive pressure under control.

signals.title: Red-zone decisions
signals.detail: Watch the throw when the first option disappears. Taking the safe exit can leave another chance to score.
signals.prompt: What should Leavitt change near the goal line?

signals.title: Defensive pressure
signals.detail: Watch the inside and outside defenders work toward the same escape point. Avoid giving the quarterback a clean running lane.
signals.prompt: What should I watch from LSU’s pass rush?

signals.title: Underneath coverage
signals.detail: Watch the linebackers and defensive backs close the short windows. A quick completion can neutralize pressure.
signals.prompt: How can LSU disrupt Ole Miss’s passing game?

signals.title: Early-down runs
signals.detail: Watch whether the backs can find steady gains before the passing situation becomes obvious. Consistency would make the next decision easier.
signals.prompt: What should LSU improve in its running game?

nextGameNote: At Ole Miss, watch red-zone decisions, underneath coverage and pressure that contains the quarterback.
